slides.title: Start with the simplest thing that works
script: Before we add anything, let's establish the **simplest version of the system**: a single user talking to a single server over HTTP. One client, one process, no scale, no redundancy.

I always start here because it forces us to agree on the **core request/response path** before we complicate it. Everything we add later — databases, caches, replicas, queues — exists to fix a specific problem this naive version has.

slides.title: Add durable storage
script: The server alone keeps everything in memory, so a restart loses all state. The first real problem to solve is **durability**, so we introduce a **database** behind the server.

The server now owns business logic and talks to the database for reads and writes. We'd choose the store based on the access pattern — a relational database for strong consistency and ad-hoc queries, or a key-value / document store if we mainly need fast lookups by id.
